newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NOL to borrow US$600 mln for APL merger.
newsitem.headline: NOL to borrow US$600 mln for APL merger.

text.p: Neptune Orient Lines (NOL) will borrow about US$600 million from banks to fund its proposed US$825 million takeover of American carrier APL Ltd, finance director Cedric Foo said on Thursday.
Foo declined to say how much interest cost the national carrier would incur as a result of the borrowings.
"Details of how we intend to refine the financing package are yet to be worked out," Foo told Reuters.
Over the weekend, NOL announced a proposal to buy all outstanding APL shares at US$33.50 each, making APL its wholly-owned subsidiary.
Both companies, with a combined fleet of 113 vessels, are expected to enjoy cost savings of at least US$130 million a year 18-24 months after the merger is completed.
The deal is subject to approval by APL shareholders and U.S. regulatory bodies.
NOL officials told a news briefing on Monday the APL purchase will be funded by internal funds and existing credit lines from 12-13 banks. NOL declined to reveal the names of the banks.
NOL also said it expected its debt to equity ratio to rise to 3.9 from two after the takeover. Its long term target was two to three.
